Issue: User snc_mid associated with down MID Server: 950591429711fa94c4aab796f053af81. No login attempts within reporting period. Script to fix it: javascript var grEAC = new GlideRecord('ecc_agent_config'); grEAC.addEncodedQuery("param_name=mid.instance.username^ecc_agent.status!=Up"); grEAC.query(); while (grEAC.next()) { //grEAC.initialize(); // grEAC.setValue('value', ''); //grEAC.autoSysFields(false); grEAC.setWorkflow(false); // grEAC.update(); //grEAC.insert(); grEAC.deleteRecord(); } Post-Fix, Validation script: javascript new MIDUserConnectivity(0).checkConnectivity(4 * (60 * 60 * 1000)); Issue: User mes_mid_ser with mid_server role not associated with a MID Server. No login attempts within reporting period. Script to fix it: javascript var all_mid_user = []; var grEAC = new GlideRecord('ecc_agent_config'); grEAC.addQuery('param_name', 'mid.instance.username'); grEAC.addQuery('ecc_agent.status', 'Up'); grEAC.query(); while (grEAC.next()) { all_mid_user.push(grEAC.getValue('value')); } // Remove mid_server role from users who are not mid.instance.username var grSUHR = new GlideRecord('sys_user_has_role'); grSUHR.addQuery('role.name', 'mid_server'); grSUHR.addQuery('user.user_name', 'NOT IN', all_mid_user.join(',')); grSUHR.query(); while (grSUHR.next()) { grSUHR.deleteRecord(); } Post-Fix, Validation script: javascript new MIDUserConnectivity(0).checkConnectivity(4 * (60 * 60 * 1000)); Main Fix: javascript // Delete MID Server usernames from ecc_agent_config where the MID Server is not Up var grEAC = new GlideRecord('ecc_agent_config'); grEAC.addQuery('param_name', 'mid.instance.username'); grEAC.addQuery('ecc_agent.status', '!=', 'Up'); grEAC.query(); while (grEAC.next()) { // grEAC.setValue('value', ''); //grEAC.autoSysFields(false); grEAC.setWorkflow(false); // grEAC.update(); grEAC.deleteRecord(); } // Get all mid.instance.username values for MID Servers that are Up var all_mid_user = []; var getMidUser = new GlideRecord('ecc_agent_config'); getMidUser.addQuery('param_name', 'mid.instance.username'); getMidUser.addQuery('ecc_agent.status', 'Up'); getMidUser.query(); while (getMidUser.next()) { all_mid_user.push(getMidUser.getValue('value')); } // Remove mid_server role from users who are not mid.instance.username var grSUHR = new GlideRecord('sys_user_has_role'); grSUHR.addQuery('role.name', 'mid_server'); grSUHR.addQuery('user.user_name', 'NOT IN', all_mid_user.join(',')); grSUHR.query(); while (grSUHR.next()) { grSUHR.deleteRecord(); } // Run Validation Job new MIDUserConnectivity(0).checkConnectivity(4 * (60 * 60 * 1000));

Table Description sys_ui_bookmark Table stores user-level bookmarks for specific pages or UI elements within the ServiceNow platform. This allows users to easily navigate to frequently accessed content. sys_ui_bookmark_group Table stores user-level bookmark Groupswithin the ServiceNow platform. This allows users to easily navigate to frequently accessed content. sys_user_presence Table tracks the online/offline status of ServiceNow users. It stores information about a user's availability, such as whether they are currently active, away, or offline. This data is used to indicate a user's presence throughout the platform. v_user_session Table provides a view of active user sessions within ServiceNow. It contains information about each user's login session, including the user, timestamp, IP address, and other relevant session details. sys_ui_list Table defines the layout and configuration of list views throughout the ServiceNow user interface. It stores the structure and customizations for how records are displayed in lists, including columns, sorting, and filtering options. sys_tiny_url Table manages shortened URL links within the ServiceNow platform. It stores the mapping between a concise URL and the full, original URL. This is used to create easily shareable links to specific pages or records in ServiceNow. isc_login_event Table records login events for users in ServiceNow. It stores information such as login time, user, IP address, and authentication details, helping to track and audit login activity. sys_ui_recent_selection Table stores the most recent selections made by users in the ServiceNow interface, allowing the platform to provide quick access to frequently used items. sys_hub_step_instance Table tracks execution instances of Flow Designer or IntegrationHub steps. It logs information about each step's state, execution time, and results for monitoring and troubleshooting flows. wf_activity Table defines individual activities within a workflow in ServiceNow. Each record represents a specific action or task, including conditions and transitions to other activities. wf_workflow_version Table stores version information of workflows in ServiceNow. Each record represents a saved version of a workflow definition, allowing tracking and rollback of workflow changes. wf_workflow_instance Table contains instances of workflow executions. It tracks the current state, start and end times, and overall progress of workflow executions for specific records. sys_journal_field Table stores journal entries such as comments and work notes added to records in ServiceNow. It enables tracking of communication and updates over a record's lifecycle. sys_audit Table logs field-level changes to records in ServiceNow. Each entry captures old and new values, user making the change, and timestamp, providing an audit history for data integrity. sys_history_set Table maintains sets of historical changes grouped together for a record. It helps organize and track changes as part of the system's auditing functionality. sys_ui_navigator_history Table stores navigation history for users in the ServiceNow UI. It keeps track of previously visited modules and pages for quick navigation. syslog Table stores system logs that capture events and messages generated by the ServiceNow platform. It includes information useful for debugging, performance monitoring, and system analysis. syslog_transaction Table logs transactional data for system operations in ServiceNow. Before you consider scripting your approval, please check out this article and Platform Academy recording about Approvals in Flow Designer. There's a good chance you don't actually need to script the approval and can just use the "Ask for Approval" Action with low-code conditions. Scripting should always be your last resort. Article: https://sn.works/CoE/FlowApproval Academy: https://sn.works/platformacademy/35 When creating approvals for Tasks, or specifically Catalog Items, the provided options for requesting approval from a specific user or group are not always sufficient to cover your use case. Sometimes you just need that extra condition to make sure the correct people may approve or reject. In the "before Flow Designer times", this would mean Scripted Approvals. The Flow Action "Ask for Approval" also allows you to script approval rules, but it's not obvious at first glance which kind of input is needed to create the approval. The introduction of Flow Variables allows us to create approvals with an absolute minimum of scripting.
The Flow Action "Ask for Approval" accepts a return value composed of several components: Ruleset Rule Who sys_id list Square brackets ([]) contain a comma-separated list of sys_ids.
text Any = Anyone approves All = All users approve Res = All responded and anyone approves % = % of users approve ## = Number of users approve

Approval Scenario Script Approved by any User ApprovesAnyU[user_sys_id,user_sys_id] Approved by 50% of Group Approves50%G[group_sys_id] Approved by 2 Users or by Group Approves2#U[user_sys_id,user_sys_id]G[group_sys_id] Rejected by all Users RejectsAllU[user_sys_id,user_sys_id] Approved or Rejected by any User ApprovesRejectsAnyU[user_sys_id] Approved by Group or Rejected by any User ApprovesAnyG[group_sys_id]OrRejectsAnyU[user_sys_id] All responded and anyone approves in Group ApprovesResG[group_sys_id]

Rulesets​ Ruleset Description Approves Approval conditions only Rejects Rejection conditions only ApprovesRejects Either approval or rejection conditions Rules​ Rule Meaning Any Any one approver can approve All All approvers must approve Res All approvers must respond and at least one approves % Percentage of approvers required # Specific number of approvers required Targets​ Code Target U Users G Groups
